body:
Rafael Mendes: Kicking off backfill plan for last 90d incidents (Hosted + Dedicated; Private only where we were primary operator). Goal is to get normalized taxonomy fields for dashboards + baseline by end of next week.

Rafael Mendes: Working sheet (tab = “Backfill 90d”) is here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/incident-inventory-and-clustering-sheet (please don’t rename columns 🙏). Mei set up filters + a “needs_review” column.

Mei Lin: Yep. Scope is 90 days ending yesterday (inclusive). We have 126 incidents in range after de-dupe (merged a few “follow-on” incident rooms). Each row needs:
- `incident_category` (v1 list)
- `impacted_surface` (Hosted API / Dedicated pools / Console / Control plane / Private)
- `primary_owner_team`
- `region` (if known)
- `contributing_factors` (optional but strongly preferred)

Mei Lin: To keep it low-cog-load: if you’re unsure between two categories, pick the best fit + add a note in `needs_review` like “torn between routing_overload vs capacity_exhaustion”. We’ll do a review pass.

Miles Thornton: +1. For backfill we’re aiming for consistency > perfection. If it was clearly multi-causal, choose the *primary* driver for category and capture secondary stuff in contributing factors.

Allison Grant: Quick reminder: please use allowed values only (dropdowns in sheet). If you type freeform we’ll spend all day cleaning. If you don’t see a value you need, flag in #eng-sre and we’ll decide whether it’s a v1 gap or a misfit.

Rafael Mendes: Proposed batch assignment (roughly 25–30 incidents each):
- Batch A (rows 2–34): @Miles Thornton
- Batch B (rows 35–67): @Aisha Bello
- Batch C (rows 68–100): @Allison Grant
- Batch D (rows 101–133): @Sergio Costa

Rafael Mendes: If anyone’s OOO, call it now and we’ll reshuffle.

Sergio Costa: I can take D. Heads up I’m slammed Tue PM but can do Wed/Thu. Also: do we want me to prioritize the ones tagged “major” for dashboard validation?

Mei Lin: Yes please. If you see any of the “major” ones missing region/tier, try to fill from the incident doc. Dashboard joins break when region is blank.

Aisha Bello: Taking Batch B. Question: for Dedicated incidents where the symptom is 429/queueing but root was autoscaler misconfig, are we labeling as `capacity_exhaustion` or `autoscaling_policy`?

Miles Thornton: For v1 we said:
- `autoscaling_policy` when the *policy/controller* is wrong or stuck (desired != actual, scale events not firing, config regression)
- `capacity_exhaustion` when fleet truly can’t supply capacity fast enough (provisioning lead time, GPU supply, quota)
If both, pick the one that would’ve prevented the impact if fixed.

Aisha Bello: Got it. I’ll follow that.

Sean Gallagher: Thanks all. Let’s be explicit about QA so we don’t end up with “looks fine” data.

Rafael Mendes: QA proposal:
1) Each batch owner completes their rows by EOD Thu.
2) Mei runs validation (allowed values, no blanks for required fields) Fri AM.
3) Spot check: 10% random sample + 10 “high-impact” incidents reviewed by Miles + Rafael.
4) Any category churn >5% (post-review changes) triggers a quick sync to clarify definitions.

Mei Lin: I can do the random sampler + validation script. I’ll add a “qa_status” column with values: `pending`, `pass`, `needs_fix`.

Allison Grant: For the spot check, can we also check that `primary_owner_team` matches the ownership map? We’ve had a bunch of “platform” vs “infra” confusion lately.

Rafael Mendes: Yes. Add to QA checklist:
- category conforms to definition
- impacted surface is sensible
- owner team aligns with ownership map (or note why it’s an exception)

Devon Price: FYI once backfill is done, I can ingest via the tagging pipeline spike work. But please keep the sheet column names identical to the incident-bot fields:
`incident_category`, `impacted_surface`, `primary_owner_team`, `customer_tier`, `region`, `contributing_factors`.

Sergio Costa: One more: do we want `customer_tier` mandatory? A lot of older incidents didn’t record it.

Aisha Bello: For SLA mapping we only really need tier on Sev1/Sev2. For Sev3 it’s nice-to-have.

Mei Lin: In the sheet tier is optional for backfill, but if it’s obvious from the ticket/Slack context please fill it. I added a quick filter view “Missing tier on Sev1/Sev2” to make that easy.

Dev Patel: Support request: if you find incidents that were driven by “customer misconfig” vs “platform issue”, please still pick the best category but add contributing factor `customer_integration` (or whatever the dropdown is). Helps us map to playbooks.

Miles Thornton: Yep, that’s a good use of contributing factors. Category is still “what broke in our world”, but contributing factors can include customer-triggered patterns.

Sean Gallagher: Timeline check:
- Thu EOD: labeling complete
- Fri: QA + fixes
- Mon: publish baseline charts (top categories + MTTR) and roll into the taxonomy dashboards
Sound right?

Rafael Mendes: Works. I’ll post a reminder Thu AM. Please @mention me if you hit an incident that genuinely doesn’t fit v1 (don’t invent new labels in-sheet).

Allison Grant: :thumbsup: starting on Batch C today.

Sergio Costa: :thumbsup: on it.

Mei Lin: I’ll drop validation results in this thread Fri once runs are done.
